title: Align tensor shapes without losing metadata
goal: Align differently ranked measurement batches while preserving requested dimensions.

selectionNotes: Align differently ranked measurement batches while preserving requested dimensions.
Verified with GA SDK/runtime and System.Numerics.Tensors11.0.0 on Windows x64. Other platforms and execution engines remain unverified.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: Canonical full-release target is .NET 11; this recipe does not establish a newer-package-on-net10 route.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Use the .NET 11 SDK for the net11.0/C#15 consumer; exact tested pins are evidence baselines.

language.name: C#
language.reason: Canonical current sample mode; the policy code requires no experimental syntax.

packages.name: System.Numerics.Tensors
packages.reason: The shipped .NET 11 package contains the release/11.0 storage and shape backport; verified with package11.0.0.

packageAssets: Canonical route: lib/net11.0/System.Numerics.Tensors.dll from package11.0.0; previous policy uses10.0.13/lib/net10.0.
platforms: Measured Windows x64 CoreCLR JIT execution. Other platforms, Native AOT and Mono are not tested.
prerequisites: SDK console project, ImplicitUsings=enable, Nullable=enable, namespace Playbook.Samples and using System.Numerics.Tensors; add the final System.Numerics.Tensors11 package containing the backport.
The fictional instrument uses dense three-channel readings. Choose exact stored dimensions or library shape equivalence before combining data.
For optional large native authoring proof: Windows x64, AllowUnsafeBlocks=true and at least 8 GiB measured free physical/commit memory. No new recurring CI/OS matrix.
constraints: Default rank-zero empties compute as [0] while retaining stored metadata. Only leading singleton padding is ignored; zero/internal dimensions remain significant. Equality is not general broadcasting. Axes follow the first effective input; caller destinations keep their requested shape.

No provider, rendering mode, workload, account or experimental API opt-in is required. NativeMemory/kernel32 resource checks are test-only system facilities, not application prerequisites. The comparison adds no target10 foundation.
stabilityLimitations: No experimental annotation or opt-in on the selected GA types. Execution proof is limited to the declared consumers and measured Windows x64 platform; global stable readiness remains PIN-967.
